rows.why: Small role: one or two plays decide this, so it's risky — we expect about 1.6 rushing yards vs the 38.5 line. We give the under 62% (needs 53% to pay at -115); recent games and the matchup both point lower
rows.why_long: Hard Rock under 38.5 at -115 needs 53% to pay; fair after the vig 50%. Averaging 1.5 over the last 4 games, lower than 38.5 in 100% of them (raw 98%, shrunk 59%). NYG allows +5% to QBs → projects 1.6 (raw 98%, shrunk 62%).
why_points: The bet: Rush yds under 38.5 at -115. To make money it has to win 53% of the time. The betting market, with the sportsbook's cut removed, gives it 50%.
Game log, most recent first: 2, 4, 0, -1. Weighted average 1.5; went lower than 38.5 in 4 of 4 games (100% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.9, so the line is 19.9 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Market: DraftKings make this side 49% once their cut is removed; Hard Rock's price needs 53%. Hard Rock charges more than the market for this side.
Matchup: NYG has allowed +5% vs the league average to QBs (already shrunk toward average for sample size).
Projection: we expect 1.6 rushing yards on average; in a typical game 0.9 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 37.6 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 98% and the matchup 98%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 59%, matchup 62%.
Bottom line: we give it 62% to win and it needs 53%. The edge is the difference: +8.0 points; that works out to about +15¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: only 4 recent games; a raw read above 90% - where these methods were most overconfident.
rows.glance_head: The under looks good: we expect about 0.9 in a typical game vs the 38.5 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.
